clue.text: Jump on this passenger vehicle: European tours popular

parts.note: a tram carries passengers along street rails

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: a native of Poland
fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a bus ride touring Europe as a popular trip to hop aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jump on this' sounds like boarding the vehicle, but it is the definition: the thing you bounce on.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is the springy frame you bounce on, so it is what you jump on.

clue.text: Weary about doctor's tone

indicators.note: about means round the outside, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: to weary is to tire
Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A patient finds the doctor's manner tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a standard abbreviation for a doctor; the 's links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the distinctive quality or colour of a sound, its characteristic tone.

clue.text: Evidence watching the Ashes, say?

definitions.note: a verb here: to evidence or bear witness

parts.note: if you are watching a match, you are at it
the Ashes is a series of Test matches; say marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A cricket fan asks for proof they were present at the Ashes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia, played as five-day Test matches.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or provide proof, the same as the verb evidence.

clue.text: More tiny fragments in elixir — so fluid?

indicators.note: as a verb, fragments means breaks into bits, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
an elixir is a magic potion

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether breaking an elixir into ever smaller bits would make it runnier.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces go into the shuffle together: MORE TINY plus POTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry in motion is an idiom for movement so graceful and smooth that it seems to flow.

clue.text: Son: a cruel, wicked criminal

indicators.note: wicked suggests something twisted and corrupted, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent laments a heartless, wicked son who has turned to crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Larcenous means given to larceny, that is theft, so it describes something criminal.

clue.text: Bay in European resort containing harbour, originally

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the resort's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of harbour

explanation.surface: A travel note about a bay in a Riviera town that has a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like a seaside bay, matching the harbour, but it means an alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay can be a recess in a wall or room, which is exactly what a niche is.

clue.text: Order another sherry: brandy overpriced initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the opening letter of each word is used

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A drinker orders another sherry and grumbles that the brandy is overpriced.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British Anti-Social Behaviour Order, a court order against nuisance conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: An ASBO is a type of court order restricting someone's behaviour, so it is an order.

clue.text: Poor fugitives finally caught

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of that word is kept

parts.note: last letter of fugitives
trapped means caught

explanation.surface: Penniless runaways are eventually captured.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped, as in strapped for cash, is informal for short of money, that is poor.

clue.text: Breakfast landlord neither starts nor finishes?

indicators.note: a word that neither starts nor finishes has lost its first and last letters

parts.note: cryptically, a landlord is one who lets a home

explanation.surface: A guest notes that the landlord never begins or finishes breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Read landlord as HOME LETTER, someone who lets out a home, then drop its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is a common breakfast dish, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Character stole awfully large car

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some rogue has shamefully made off with a big vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a wealthy district of London; a Chelsea tractor is British slang for a big 4x4 driven on city streets.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase mocks oversized off-road vehicles used for school runs in town, so it names a large car.

clue.text: Joint that goes to a bishop's head!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a corner joint made by cutting two pieces at an angle

definitions.text: that goes to a bishop's head
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the tall pointed headdress worn by a bishop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to a bishop's head' sounds like drink going to someone's head, but it is literally the hat sitting on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a carpentry joint at an angle and a bishop's ceremonial headgear.

clue.text: Jockey chose rare animal bred for speed

indicators.note: as a verb, to jockey is to manoeuvre and jostle for position, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider picks an unusual mount bred to be fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' looks like the rider in the scene, but it is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoroughbred racehorses are bred specifically for speed on the track.

clue.text: Extra book

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a spare, a substitute held back
second meaning: to make a booking in advance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a noun but works as the verb meaning to arrange in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve is an extra or spare kept back, and to reserve a table is to book it.

clue.text: Top trimmed beef stuffed with prunes

indicators.note: something stuffed with a filling holds that filling inside it
trimmed means cut back at the edges, so the word loses both its outer letters

parts.note: taken as written, before trimming
prunes as a verb: cuts back, clips

explanation.surface: A recipe line: lean beef filled with dried plums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prunes' looks like the fruit but is the verb for cutting back. BEEF trimmed leaves EE, filled with CLIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To top something is to surpass it, and to eclipse is to outshine or overshadow.

clue.text: Thrashing received, might this selection be preferred in volleyball team?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a caning of six strokes, the old school punishment

definitions.text: might this selection be preferred in volleyball team?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a volleyball side fields six players, so you would pick your top six

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase was the traditional British school caning; read literally it is a selection of six top players, the size of a volleyball side.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a punishment of six cane strokes and, literally, the six finest picks.

clue.text: Fairytale with a giant?

parts.note: surface reading: a children's story such as Jack and the Beanstalk
setter's reading: a fairytale is an unbelievable fib, and a giant is very high, so the fib is lofty

explanation.walkthrough: Fairytale here means an implausible lie, and the giant supplies the adjective for an exaggerated one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an idiom for an exaggerated, unbelievable account, a fairytale in the sense of a fib.

clue.text: Features cool in space rocket

parts.note: a film that features an actor stars that actor
fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A film showcases something cool inside a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A starship is a science-fiction spacecraft for travel between stars, a kind of space rocket.

clue.text: Approved accessing Scottish peak in lift

indicators.note: accessing means getting into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
approved as correct, right

explanation.surface: Someone gets permission to reach a Highland summit by ski lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like a ski lift on the mountain, but it is the verb meaning to cheer up.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift someone's mood is to brighten it, both meaning to make more cheerful.

clue.text: A curry in pie, a Greek dish

indicators.note: in places the first part inside the following word

parts.note: a tart is a pastry pie
taken as written
masala is a spiced curry dish or mix
taken as written

explanation.surface: A menu oddity: a curry baked in a pie described as Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sits between the curry and the pie, so the curry with its article goes inside; the last 'a' trails after.
explanation.definitionFit: Taramasalata is a Greek dip or meze made from fish roe.

clue.text: Family into great outdoor activity

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the first piece is placed within the second

parts.note: great means large, big
one's kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A household is keen on the great outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Biking, riding a bicycle, is a typical pastime done outside.

clue.text: Minor act of neglect

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a snub, a pointed disregard

explanation.walkthrough: The two phrases read like one: a small instance of neglect.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means small or trivial; the noun means an insult by being ignored.

clue.text: Great revolutionary and Territorials meet on water

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the existing order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A famous rebel and some reservist soldiers rendezvous on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great revolutionary' looks like a famous rebel, but revolutionary is the shuffle signal on GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a sporting meeting of rowing or sailing races, held on water.

clue.text: Use a mask, did you say?

definitions.note: a noun here, as in 'to no avail'

indicators.note: asking what someone said points to how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: a veil is a face covering, a kind of mask

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether they heard right: wear a face covering?
explanation.definitionFit: Avail means benefit or usefulness, as in 'to no avail', meaning of no use.

clue.text: Talk about an obsequious character!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a spiel is a glib line of talk
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark about some fawning creep.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel, after the eager dog, is figuratively a fawning, servile person.

clue.text: Stew: tiny bit unfinished — that's a problem

indicators.note: unfinished means without its ending, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a hotpot is a meat and potato stew, as in Lancashire hotpot
an atom is a tiny particle

explanation.surface: A cook frets that the stew is not quite done and that is an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lancashire hotpot is a slow-cooked British meat and potato casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a controversial issue nobody wants to handle, a tricky problem.

clue.text: Cup of tea taken in Bayreuth in Germany

indicators.note: taken in means held within, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: letters straddling the end of Bayreuth, in and the start of Germany

explanation.surface: Having a cuppa in the Bavarian festival town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup of tea' is not a drink: it is the idiom for something you like, as in 'not my cup of tea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is your thing is something you enjoy, which is what being your cup of tea means.

clue.text: Bet money at the Curragh, some years ago?

definitions.text: money at the Curragh, some years ago?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Irish pound, Ireland's currency before the euro

explanation.walkthrough: The Curragh is Ireland's main racecourse, so the surface reads as betting there; the old Irish currency was called the punt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a wager and was also the name of the Irish pound before 2002.

clue.text: Scenarist wary about getting into trouble

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the shuffled piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a plight is a predicament, trouble

indicators.note: about can mean in a disordered state, all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A screenwriter is nervous about landing in hot water.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenarist writes scenarios or scripts, much as a playwright writes plays.
